approach:
Root cause: landing, history and attribution rules are derived from the happy-path commit shape (the job's own commits), and the only guard is planner/critic prose (planner.md:16, critic.md:14). Nothing runs where readings are accepted, so jobs 20261024-153908-1rve, 20261024-154552-e65v and 20261025-012657-hac3 each got readings whose criteria never required a branch with an intervention commit, a records-only commit and the job landing. Fix: one pure check, `check_history_fixture(reading)`, in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs, added as one `step!` line in `refusing_check` right after `check_code_survey`. Revision changes after the critic's findings: (a) bare `landing` is no longer a trigger; (b) the file trigger matches full crate paths of the real classification code (not bare file names); (c) refusal and acceptance tests are built in the shape of each of the three source jobs; (d) the athena-context change stays inside that crate; (e) the doc comment and CHANGELOG say the check has no reader rule line, and why.

Gate: the same conditions as `check_code_survey` (capability set, no question, class `code` or `tests`, at least one Behavior criterion), factored into one private helper.

Trigger (either): (1) a non-Delete deliverable whose full path is one of crates/athena-core/src/land.rs, crates/athena-core/src/commits.rs, crates/athena-core/src/reconcile.rs, crates/athena-gate/src/invariant.rs, crates/athena-gate/src/history.rs, crates/athena-gate/src/attribution.rs, crates/athena-git/src/attrs.rs. These are where `pr_commits` (land.rs:212), `classify_commit` (land.rs:229), `classify_pre_merge` (invariant.rs:320), `classify` (attrs.rs:46) and the merge-method-follows-commit-shape test (reconcile.rs:652) live. crates/athena-data/src/history.rs (a record schema) and crates/athena-gate/src/reconcile.rs (usage records) are not on the list. (2) Any criterion text (any kind) holds one of these whole-word phrases, matched with the existing `has_phrase` on lowercase, white-space-collapsed, straight-apostrophe text: `commit shape`, `commit shapes`, `commit-shape`, `pr_commits`, `classify_commit`, `classify_pre_merge`, `history check`, `attribution check`, `records-only commit`, `records only commit`, `trailer`, `trailers`, `--history`, `--attribution`, `--pr-head`. The bare word `landing` triggers nothing. `has_phrase` only tests `char::is_alphanumeric` on each side (reading.rs:3752-3757), so `_` and `-` count as boundaries; the doc comment and the tests state this.

Satisfaction: some Behavior criterion whose normalised text has `realistic`, `fixture`, `intervention commit`, `records-only commit` (or `records only commit`) and `job landing` (or `job's landing`). Otherwise the check bails with 'the reading was refused because ...', naming what triggered it and giving an example criterion.

Estimate: HISTORY.txt (last 200 commits) lists 15 commits that touched a listed source file (land.rs 8, reconcile.rs 3 more, commits.rs 1 more, athena-gate attribution/history 3 more; counted from the path lines I read). That is 7.5% as an upper bound for the file trigger, since not every such job is a code reading with a behavior criterion and no fixture. The phrase triggers add only commits already in that count. The declaration is 'expected 7% of newly refused readings', labelled an unmeasured estimate that the replay at verification measures.

The check reads only the Reading: no model call, no repository, no records, no network. It does not touch land.rs, gh.rs, invariant.rs, commits.rs or athena-git, so no classification function changes and no commit-shape table applies to this plan (see risks).

decisions.choice: Enforce at the reading-stage gate: `step!(check_history_fixture(reading));` right after `check_code_survey` in `refusing_check`.
decisions.reason: All three failures began when a reading was accepted whose criteria never required a branch with more than job commits. `refusing_check` is the one seam every reading passes (`check_reading_acceptance` at reading.rs:3199, `check_reading_text` for `athena check-reading` and the replay, and `Athena::read`). The step name comes from `stringify!`. The new line does not sit between the governance/outcome_state/environment_reach steps whose adjacency tests pin them.

rejected.option: Re-land the pr_commits classification or the trailer cutover work (land.rs, gh.rs, invariant.rs, commits.rs)
rejected.why: Those are the instances, and the brief drops them. Another fix to one classification leaves the next landing rule free to be tested only against job commits.

rejected.option: More planner/critic prose or a planner-side check
rejected.why: The guidance already exists as prose (planner.md:16, critic.md:14, lib.rs test at 490) and failed three times. Those prompts are out of scope, and the planner has no mechanical gate.

rejected.option: A rule line in the reader prompt
rejected.why: The reader prompt has 3 tokens of headroom (budget reader: 1997 of 2000 in docs/system-facts.md) and the briefs.rs test pins 7 rule lines. The briefs.rs list (briefs.rs:4411) only asserts that named checks have rules, so it does not fail for a missing one. The gap is stated openly in the check's doc comment and the CHANGELOG instead, and the refusal message with its example criterion is how readers learn the rule.

decisions.choice: Do not trigger on the bare word `landing`. Trigger on commit-classification phrases (`commit shape`, `pr_commits`, `history check`, `attribution check`, `records-only commit`, `trailer`, `--history`, `--attribution`, `--pr-head`, `classify_commit`, `classify_pre_merge`) or on the classification source files.
decisions.reason: Finding 2: about 12 of the last 200 HISTORY.txt subjects say 'landing' (6e7fd3a stack-aware rebase for landing, e15681f FIFO LandingQueue, 47cadfa landing time, c7c4157 wait for the early CI run before the landing commit, 1676fe9 config edits not only at landing). Their behavior criteria are about queues, timing and CI waits, not commit shape, and would be refused for a fixture that does not apply. A test pins that a queue/timing/CI-wait criterion is not refused.

rejected.option: Keep `landing` as a trigger, as in the first plan
rejected.why: Common-word false positive; it also makes the declared share too low.
c7c4157 ('pushing the landing commit') is a CI-wait change, not a classification rule.

decisions.choice: The file trigger matches full crate paths of the classification code (land.rs, commits.rs and reconcile.rs in athena-core; invariant.rs, history.rs and attribution.rs in athena-gate; attrs.rs in athena-git). It does not match bare file names and does not trigger on gh.rs or gh/landing.rs.
decisions.reason: Finding 3: a bare `history.rs` also matches crates/athena-data/src/history.rs, a record-schema module. The listed files are where the classification functions are (land.rs:212 and :229, invariant.rs:320, attrs.rs:46, reconcile.rs:652) and where job hac3 changed commits.rs and athena-git. A test shows athena-data/src/history.rs does not trigger. gh.rs holds PR creation and CI polling, so a gh.rs job that changes a landing check is caught by the phrase triggers instead.

rejected.why: False positive on the athena-data history module.
Would refuse most unrelated code jobs.
It reconciles usage records (module doc line 1), not commit shape.

decisions.choice: Tests are built from the shape of each of the three source jobs: 1rve and e65v (deliverables land.rs, gh.rs, invariant.rs, records-history.md, CHANGELOG.md; criteria about pr_commits, the reconcile merge method and the commit shape) and hac3 (deliverables commits.rs, manage.rs, an athena-git file, status.rs, auditor.rs, gate files; criteria about trailers after C0). Each is refused without the realistic-fixture criterion and accepted with it. The same shapes go into the refusal corpus.
decisions.reason: Finding 3 and criterion 3 ('for the cause and not only for one job'): the check must be shown on the class, not on one invented `land::` criterion. The brief records only the deliverable lists and the nature of each job, so the readings are rebuilt from that, and the corpus `source` text says so.

decisions.choice: Factor the gate conditions of `check_code_survey` (reading.rs:3913-3920) into a private helper used by both checks.
decisions.reason: One definition of 'a code reading with a behavior criterion'. The existing `code_survey_does_not_apply_outside_its_gate` covers it.

decisions.choice: The satisfying criterion must be a Behavior criterion carrying `realistic`, `fixture` and the three shapes. The three shapes are the ones the brief fixes; the retry-after-block landing is not required.
decisions.reason: A fixture belongs to a test, so only a Behavior criterion is a test demonstration. A fourth shape would raise the refusal share beyond the declared estimate, and the planner prose already asks for it. The shared CutoverFixture by name alone is not accepted: its documented history does not by itself include an intervention commit.

rejected.why: It cannot show a test on a branch.
It would let a rule pass without the shapes.
Outside the brief's three shapes; raises the share.

decisions.reason: Finding 5: the frame phrase is already asserted and the step line is pinned in reading.rs; reading another crate's source in reverse dependency order adds little. This keeps lib.rs a deliverable with a minimal, real edit.

rejected.why: Reverse dependency order for a check already pinned in reading.rs.
Out of scope and would move the budget lines.

risks.risk: Over-refusal: a code job that touches a listed source for an unrelated reason (for example land.rs for a queue or timing change) is refused and costs a reader retry. HISTORY.txt shows land.rs touched by several such jobs.
risks.mitigation: The file list is the exact classification code, the phrase list has no bare `landing`, and the gate is code/tests with a behavior criterion. The refusal message gives an example criterion, so one retry fixes it. The share is declared (7%, estimate) and the replay at verification measures it; above 10% the replay holds the job unless a share is declared.

risks.risk: The reader cannot satisfy the check because it does not know the wording, and there is no reader rule line (the reader has 3 tokens of headroom).
risks.mitigation: The error text gives an exact example criterion. Spelling variants (hyphen or space, `job's landing`, curly apostrophe) are accepted. The doc comment and CHANGELOG say openly that the refusal is how readers learn the rule.

risks.risk: A criterion names the three shapes but the test uses a poor fixture, since the check is lexical and cannot read a negation.
risks.mitigation: The limit is stated in the doc comment. The criterion must be a Behavior criterion, and the planner/verifier still judge the fixture.

risks.risk: An existing test builds a code/tests reading that holds a trigger phrase or a listed path and now fails.
risks.mitigation: The producer searches the tests modules and crates/*/tests for such readings (expected: only ENGM) and runs the full `cargo test --locked`.

risks.risk: A corpus case is refused by an earlier check, so its expected check name is wrong; Accept cases using a deliverable absent from `repo_files()` would be refused by the repo check.
risks.mitigation: Cases start from `base_reading` with one field changed; code cases set class code, a Behavior criterion and a `Code survey:` assumption so check_code_survey passes first. Accept cases use phrase triggers and the existing deliverable reading.rs; the Refuse cases for listed source paths are refused by my check before the repo-file check runs. The check order is never changed to fit a case.

risks.risk: This plan changes a reading gate, not a landing or history rule, so the commit-shape table rule does not apply, and no classification function is changed. If the producer touched land.rs or athena-git by mistake the scope would widen.
risks.mitigation: Criterion 7 has the verifier read the diff and confirm that only the five planned files changed. The producer still runs the full `cargo test --locked`, which covers every crate that calls those functions.

demonstrations.method: New unit tests in the reading.rs tests module, driven through production `check_reading_acceptance` and `refusing_check` using the existing helpers `code_reading`, `add_behavior`, `accept` and `refuser`. (a) `history_fixture_refuses_a_rule_tested_only_on_job_commits`: a code reading with the SURVEY assumption and a Behavior criterion such as 'Run `cargo test -p athena-core land::`: pr_commits accepts the job commits' is refused with `refuser == Some("check_history_fixture")`; the error holds 'was refused', 'realistic-branch fixture', 'intervention commit', 'records-only commit', 'job landing'. After adding the Behavior criterion 'Run `cargo test -p athena-core --test reconcile`: the realistic-branch fixture holds an intervention commit, a records-only commit and the job landing, and the rule classifies each', `refuser` is None and `accept` is Ok. Spelling variants (`records only commit`, `job's landing`, curly apostrophe, extra white space) are accepted; a Content-kind fixture criterion, a criterion missing one shape, and a criterion without 'fixture' stay refused. (b) The three source-job shapes, each refused without and accepted with the fixture criterion: `history_fixture_job_1rve_shape` (deliverables land.rs, gh.rs, invariant.rs, docs/design/records-history.md, CHANGELOG.md; criterion on pr_commits content classification), `history_fixture_job_e65v_shape` (land.rs, invariant.rs; criterion that the reconcile merge method follows the commit shape), `history_fixture_job_hac3_shape` (commits.rs, manage.rs, an athena-git attrs.rs, status.rs, auditor.rs; criterion that no Athena trailers are written after C0), plus a criterion-only trigger test where the deliverables are manage.rs and status.rs and the criterion says 'trailer'. (c) `history_fixture_refusal_needs_the_step_line` greps the `refusing_check` body for the step and fails if it is removed.
demonstrations.observes: A code reading for a landing, history or attribution rule, in the shape of each of the three source jobs, is refused with an actionable message when no criterion names a realistic-branch fixture with the three shapes, and is accepted once one does.
